Hi Olivia / Michael,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps to keep momentum: 

1) Key takeaways from call
- Primary workload: financial document summarization + customer support triage (mixed short/long prompts, ~2k tokens/session).
- Latency target: 200–300ms p95 for short queries; acceptable up to 1.2s for long-context generation.
- Throughput: steady 250 qps during peak (batching likely helps).
- Data sensitivity: customer PII, SOC2 + vendor review required (you mentioned procurement timeline ~3–4 weeks).

2) Suggested immediate evals
- Model candidates: Llama-3-Chat-13B (fp16 baseline) for best quality/latency balance; Mistral-Instruct-7B and Falcon-40B-ggml quantized variants for cost/perf comparison.
- Quantization/throughput knobs to test: AWQ (4-bit) and GPTQ (4-bit), plus experimental FP8 runs (if you want to test performance on Dedicated).
- Prompt set: I'll share a 120-example sample covering short support replies, structured summaries, and the longer reconciliation flows.

3) Next steps
- Action: I will share a trade study (AWQ vs GPTQ vs FP8) + prompt set by EOD Friday.
- You: send the redacted sample documents you mentioned for fidelity tests (we can sign an MoU/NDA if needed).
- Schedule: propose a 45-minute technical eval session the week of Mar 1 to review initial regressions and throughput numbers.

Attachments: preliminary quantization trade-study (PDF) and a sample prompt set CSV.

Thanks — happy to run any of these as hosted POC or on Dedicated nodes depending on your procurement preference.

Best,

Hi Olivia / Michael — attaching the trade study and prompt set sample as promised. Notes below to help interpret the results.

Attachment notes (20270226-quantization-trade-study.pdf):
- Tested models: Llama-3-Chat-13B (fp16 baseline), Mistral-Instruct-7B (fp16 baseline), Falcon-40B-ggml (fp16 baseline).
- Quant strategies: AWQ-4 (reconstructed 4-bit), GPTQ-4 (group-wise), FP8 experimental run (where supported).
- Hardware: tests run on Dedicated A100s (fp16/FP8 paths) and on a RTX6000-like instance for AWQ/GPTQ CPU fallback tests.

Key findings (summary):
- Quality: Llama-3-Chat-13B fp16 baseline has the highest pass-rate on our financial-phrasing evals (~92% on the 120-sample set).
- AWQ-4 on Llama-13B: ~2–3% drop in strict-fidelity metrics (currency/precision checks) but 2.5x throughput improvement. Hallucination rate increased slightly on edge cases (0.8% absolute increase).
- GPTQ-4: similar throughput gains but slightly higher fidelity than AWQ on Llama (1.5% drop vs fp16). GPTQ tended to preserve numeric fidelity better in our tests.
- FP8: where supported, FP8 gave the best latency and throughput (3–4x vs fp16) with negligible quality drop on Llama-13B (<1%), but FP8 support is limited and requires Dedicated GPU kernel availability — not available on CPU fallbacks.

Recommendations for FinWave initial POC:
- If quality (numerical fidelity) is the primary constraint: start with Llama-3-Chat-13B fp16 on Dedicated; test GPTQ-4 as the conservative quant option.
- If cost/throughput is the priority with acceptable small fidelity tradeoffs: AWQ-4 on Llama-13B or FP8 on Dedicated (if you can commit to Dedicated hardware).
- Practical path: run a 2-week A/B eval: fp16 baseline vs GPTQ-4 vs AWQ-4, instrumented with the 120-sample prompt set + your 30 redacted docs. We'll collect the following metrics: strict-fidelity, hallucination rate, latency p95, tokens/sec, and cost per 1M tokens.

Related links (benchmarks and eval dashboards) included in the PDF. Prompt set sample included as CSV (30 examples here; full 120 prompt set in Drive once we get your redacted docs).

Quick note on regression monitoring: Redwood Optimize can run continuous evals on your prompt set post-deploy and alert on fidelity regressions above a threshold you set (we can pre-configure cost-aware rollbacks).

If helpful, Rishi can scope an infra/benchmark plan for the Mar 1 session.

Best,
Marissa
